items.item_text: Pharmacist Board Certification [e.g., Board Certified Transplant Pharmacist (BCTXP), Board Certified Pharmacotherapy Specialist (BCPS), Board Certified Ambulatory Care Pharmacist (BCACP), or Certified Specialty Pharmacist (CSP)]
Completion of a Post Graduate Year Two (PGY2) Residency in area of position emphasis (i.e., Transplant), or five (5) years of experience with similar clinical practice

The Solid Organ Transplant Pharmacist position focuses on patient care within both the inpatient and ambulatory care spaces. This Clinical Pharmacist primarily serves kidney and liver transplant recipient patients along their continuum of care in the hospital and during post-discharge follow-up. This role may help additional transplant patients subject to new transplant service lines established via CPA.

The Clinical Pharmacist is responsible for directing and maintaining drug therapy across the continuum of care, providing comprehensive service-based monitoring on select services, as well as focused monitoring in the areas of supportive care/symptom management, antimicrobial management, anticoagulation, and parenteral nutrition therapy. The Clinical Pharmacist continuously seeks out interventions and offers suggestions on individualized medication regimens.
20% - Support Staff and Other Duties Assigned

The Pharmacist is an integral member of the health care team, also contributing to drug distribution activities, providing drug information, serving as a preceptor to pharmacy students and residents, conducting clinical research, and participating in department and hospital committees, task forces and work groups. They foster excellent interdepartmental relationships and provide quality and cost-effective pharmaceutical care to all patients, employees and medical staff of UCDMC.

To provide quality pharmaceutical services to the patients, employees and medical staff of UC Davis Health. A Staff Pharmacist is an integral member of the health care team, responsible for drug therapy monitoring, distribution, drug information, and precepting pharmacy students and residents, conducting clinical research, participating in Department and Hospital Committees, task forces and work groups and fostering excellent interdepartmental relationships.

Problem-solving skills to independently recognize and define a problem, identify the resources available to help solve the problem, create and implement viable solutions, and follow through to ensure the problem is resolved to the satisfaction of all parties.
Ability to oversee technicians and establish priorities of workflow
